scalar.method: 100 timed plain compilations and one warmup per fresh guest, ABCDE/EDCBA, CPU2, icount0, x-pcrel=false. Configuration flags recorded in command/summary files.
scalar.conclusion: The u-mode CPU switch alone accounts for the platform/plain speed difference. Adding the remaining CPU, machine and kernel switches has no resolved benefit in these two samples. This is an emulator configuration control, not a comparison of capability security costs.
scalar.explanation: Legacy scalar stores invoke the remove-capability helper unconditionally; u-mode uses the TLB store hook when necessary. Separate stock/u-mode profiles also show much less MMU refill and jump-cache clearing in the fork, consistent with its pre-existing page-specific SFENCE.VMA implementation; a controlled full-flush reversal remains pending.
